sections.h2: Where is the Platte County, MO Recorder of Deeds office?
sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds is in the Platte County Administration Building, 415 Third St., Room 035, Platte City, MO 64079. The main number is (816) 858-3326, and the elected Recorder, Christopher L. Wright, also lists (816) 858-1832. Mr. Wright was first elected in November 2022.

Hours differ by task. The office is open from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. for searching records and making copies, including over the lunch hour. Documents are recorded between 9:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. The county's posted closures for the rest of 2026 are Thursday and Friday, November 26 and 27, and December 24 and 25.

sections.h2: What does the Platte County recorder do when a house is sold?
sections.html:
The office keeps the public land records for the county. Its stated duties are recording real estate transactions, filing state and federal tax liens, keeping military discharge documents and issuing marriage licenses. For a sale, the signed deed goes on record here once the buyer's closing is complete, and the lender's release of an old deed of trust is recorded the same way after a payoff.

Uniform Commercial Code filings have gone through the Missouri Secretary of State since July 1, 2001, so they are not recorded in Platte City. Aside from the DD214 disclaimer form, you do not need a formal open records request to get documents from the recorder. Call or email, and the staff will help.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Platte County?
sections.html:
A standard document costs $26 for the first page and $3 for each added page. The county says a statewide statutory increase on August 28, 2026 raised fees for recorded documents, marriage licenses and plats, and that date has passed. Overpayments are not refunded, so ask the office for the total before you mail a check.

A document that releases or assigns more than one item carries $5 for each extra item. Source: Platte County Recorder Fees.

sections.h2: What makes a Platte County document non-standard?
sections.html:
A document that does not meet the Recorders Association of Missouri formatting rules costs $25 more, which is the difference between the $26 and $51 first-page fees. The standards took effect January 1, 2002, and they are short enough to check before you sign.

  • 8.5 by 11 inch paper, white or light, 20-pound, with no watermarks or logos.
  • Black or dark ink on one side only, type no smaller than 8 point.
  • A clear top 3 inches on the first page only, kept for the recorder's certification.
  • Margins of at least three-quarters of an inch elsewhere.
  • Every signature with a typed, stamped or printed name beneath it.

The first page must carry the title, date, grantors with marital status, grantees, any statutory addresses and the legal description. Grantor and grantee must be labeled with those words so the document can be indexed, and a street address does not count as a legal description. Documents signed before 2002, military papers, documents signed abroad, court judgments and certified copies are exempt. See the county formatting page.

sections.h2: Can I record or search Platte County records online?
sections.html:
Yes. The county sends searchers to its iRecord portal at plattemo.icounty.com, and the same site hosts the free Record Notification Service. After you register for a free account, you enter criteria you choose and receive an email each time a deed matching it is recorded in the office.

That alert is handy for an owner who wants to know the moment a deed on their own property is recorded. Fees for online searching and printing are set by the portal, so check the site or ask the office before you rely on a figure. The county also states that its recorder data is not official and is not a substitute for advice from a licensed professional.

sections.h2: Does Platte County charge a transfer tax when a deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The county's fee schedule lists recording and copy charges only, with no line for a transfer tax. For a question about taxes owed on a sale, ask the title company or a Missouri attorney, and call the recorder at (816) 858-3326 if you want to know what the office will collect when it accepts the deed.

Property tax is separate and sits with the Collector. The Platte County Collector's statements are due on receipt and become delinquent after December 31, and the closing agent confirms the current year before the deed is sent for recording.

sections.h2: What does Platte County's size mean for recording?
sections.html:
Platte County is part of the Kansas City metro area, and it is a busy recording market. Census QuickFacts counts 114,400 people and 47,969 housing units as of July 1, 2025, with a median owner-occupied home value of $345,100 and 425 building permits in 2025. Those numbers sit well above Pike County and Polk County in the same table.

The county was organized on December 31, 1838, and its courthouse in Platte City is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Today the recorder works from the Administration Building with a deputy staff and a chief of staff. Plan to submit a deed early in the day, because recording hours stop at 4:00 p.m. Source: Census QuickFacts.

faqs.q: How much is the first page of a deed in Platte County?
faqs.a: A standard document costs $26.00 for the first page, and each added page costs $3.00. A document that fails the formatting standards costs $51.00 for the first page.

faqs.q: What hours does the Platte County Recorder record documents?
faqs.a: Documents are recorded from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The office is open from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. for searches and copies.

faqs.q: Where do I send a deed in Platte County?
faqs.a: Take or send it to the Recorder of Deeds, 415 Third St., Room 035, Platte City, MO 64079. Call (816) 858-3326 first to confirm the total fee, since overpayments are not refunded.

faqs.q: Can Platte County alert me when a deed is recorded?
faqs.a: Yes. Register for a free account at plattemo.icounty.com, add your criteria in the Record Notification Service, and the office emails you whenever a matching deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Does the recorder file UCC statements in Platte County?
faqs.a: No. Uniform Commercial Code filings have been handled by the Missouri Secretary of State since July 1, 2001, though a fixture filing on real estate on the approved form is priced at $26.00 for the first page.
